gp.text: Gross profit for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $8,720,672, or 51.6% of revenue, compared to $6,939,793, or 47.1% of revenue, for the three months ended June 30, 2025, an increase of $1,780,879, or 25.7%, and gross-margin expansion of approximately 4.5 percentage points. The improvement in gross margin primarily reflected a higher proportion of full-price sales and reduced inventory-liquidation activity relative to the prior-year period, partially offset by higher fulfillment costs.

cor.heading: Cost of Revenues
cor.text:
Cost of revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $8,187,623, an increase of $390,915, or 5.0%, compared to $7,796,708 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Cost of revenue consisted of $5,943,978 of product cost in the 2026 period, compared to $5,862,348 in the 2025 period, and $2,243,645 of fulfillment cost in the 2026 period, compared to $1,934,360 in the 2025 period. Product cost increased 1.4% on revenue growth of 14.7%, reflecting the improvement in realized pricing described above, while fulfillment cost increased 16.0%, reflecting higher direct-to-consumer unit volume and returns and higher shipping costs.

Gross profit for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $8,720,672, or 51.6% of revenue, compared to $6,939,793, or 47.1% of revenue, for the three months ended June 30, 2025, an increase of $1,780,879, or 25.7%, and gross-margin expansion of approximately 4.5 percentage points. The improvement in gross margin primarily reflected a higher proportion of full-price sales and reduced inventory-liquidation activity relative to the prior-year period, partially offset by higher fulfillment costs.

Operating Expenses . Total operating expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $7,834,742, an increase of $978,684, or 14.5%, compared to $6,856,058 for the three months ended June 30, 2025.

oi.heading: Income from Operations
oi.text:
As a result of the foregoing, the Company generated income from operations of $885,930 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to income from operations of $83,735 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, an improvement of $802,195.

Total other income (expense), net for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was an expense of $37,115, compared to income of $184,226 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, an unfavorable change of $221,341. The change primarily reflected the absence in the 2026 period of a $406,719 gain recognized in the prior-year period on the reversal of a previously recorded loss on settlement, partially offset by lower interest expense.

Interest Expense. Interest expense for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $102,818, a decrease of $8,467, or 7.6%, compared to $111,285 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, reflecting lower average outstanding borrowings under the Company’s credit facilities during the 2026 period.

Loss on Settlement. There was no loss on settlement for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The three months ended June 30, 2025 included a $406,719 gain reflecting the reversal of a loss on settlement that had been recorded in the three months ended March 31, 2025.

Other Income (Expense).

opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Total operating expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $14,682,966, an increase of $710,530, or 5.1%, compared to $13,972,436 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase reflected higher sales and marketing expense in the second quarter and higher research and development expense, partially offset by the full-period benefit of the workforce reductions and organizational restructuring completed during the first half of 2025 and the transition of the Company’s third-party marketplace business to a distributor model, which shifted the related fulfillment, advertising, and marketing costs to the distributor partner.

General and Administrative. General and administrative expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $3,250,373, a decrease of $41,203, or 1.3%, compared to $3,291,576 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Higher professional, audit, and compliance costs associated with the Company becoming a reporting company under the Exchange Act were more than offset by the absence of restructuring-related costs incurred in the prior-year period.

Sales and Marketing. Sales and marketing expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $8,301,529, an increase of $616,795, or 8.0%, compared to $7,684,734 for the six months ended June 30, 2025.

rd.text: Research and Development. Research and development expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $428,246, an increase of $17,893, or 4.4%, compared to $410,353 for the three months ended June 30, 2025.

sm.text: Sales and Marketing. Sales and marketing expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $4,551,367, an increase of $854,191, or 23.1%, compared to $3,697,176 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Sales and marketing expense as a percentage of revenue was 26.9% in the 2026 period compared to 25.1% in the 2025 period. The increase reflected higher advertising and marketing expense, higher sales commissions as a greater proportion of the Company’s European wholesale accounts are serviced by independent sales agencies rather than in-house sales personnel, and higher selling costs associated with the increased direct-to-consumer volume.

ga.text: General and Administrative. General and administrative expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $1,730,675, a decrease of $125,071, or 6.7%, compared to $1,855,746 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease primarily reflected the absence of restructuring-related costs incurred in the prior-year period in connection with the Company’s 2025 workforce reductions, partially offset by higher professional, legal, audit, and compliance costs, including costs associated with the Company becoming a reporting company under the Exchange Act.

The change primarily reflected the absence in the 2026 period of a $406,719 gain recognized in the prior-year period on the reversal of a previously recorded loss on settlement, partially offset by lower interest expense.

tax.text: The Company recorded a provision for income taxes of $248,422 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a benefit from income tax of $675,424 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The provision for the 2026 period reflects the application of the Company’s estimated annual effective tax rate to pre-tax income, taking into account the Company’s valuation allowance position, and represents an effective tax rate of 29.27%. The benefit in the prior-year period reflected the Company’s pre-tax results and interim tax accounting for that period and did not recur.

net.heading: Net Income (Loss)
net.text: As a result of the foregoing, the Company recorded net income of $600,393 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to net income of $943,385 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of $342,992. The decrease occurred notwithstanding the $802,195 improvement in income from operations, because the prior-year period included a $406,719 gain on the reversal of a loss on settlement and an income tax benefit of $675,424, neither of which recurred in the 2026 period.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $929,993, compared to net cash provided by operating activities of $287,372 for the six months ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of $1,217,365. The decrease primarily reflected changes in working capital, including a $2,925,221 reduction in accounts payable and accrued expenses as the Company paid down vendor balances that had been elevated at December 31, 2025, compared to a $2,067,020 increase in the prior-year period, together with a $394,810 increase in prepaid expenses, a $493,683 increase in inventory, a $480,844 increase in accounts receivable and a $417,247 decrease in customer deposits. These uses were partially offset by a $1,903,673 decrease in inventory in transit as in-transit goods were received into inventory, and by the Company’s net income of $1,072,996 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to a net loss of $768,710 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Non-cash items in the 2026 period included $313,065 deferred taxes, $203,761 of depreciation and amortization, $56,037 of amortization of debt issuance costs, $91,197 of stock-based compensation, and $29,935 of credit loss expense.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text: As of June 30, 2026, the Company had working capital of $17,188,710, calculated as total current assets of $31,647,433 less total current liabilities of $14,458,723. This compares to working capital of $16,425,904 as of December 31, 2025, calculated as total current assets of $36,298,372 less total current liabilities of $19,872,468, an increase of $762,806. Current assets decreased $4,650,939, primarily reflecting a $3,964,356 decrease in cash and a $1,903,673 decrease in inventory in transit as in-transit goods were received into inventory, partially offset by increases in prepaid expenses, inventory, and accounts receivable. Current liabilities decreased $5,413,745, primarily reflecting a $2,925,221 reduction in accounts payable and accrued expenses, which had been elevated at December 31, 2025 in connection with the timing of inventory receipts and vendor payments, a $2,143,706 reduction in the net carrying amount of the Company’s line of credit, and a $417,247 decrease in customer deposits.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $16,908,295, an increase of $2,171,794, or 14.7%, compared to $14,736,501 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase reflected higher direct-to-consumer volume on the Company’s 2026 product line, a full quarter of sales through the Company’s marketplace distributor partner compared to a prior-year quarter that was disrupted by the transition of the Company’s third-party marketplace business to that partner, and sales to distributor partners added in international markets over the past year, partially offset by lower European revenue. The current period also reflected a higher proportion of full-price direct-to-consumer sales, whereas the prior-year period included a greater proportion of inventory-liquidation and clearance-related sales, which contributed to improved realized pricing and gross margin, as discussed below.
